title: Epitaxial NbN-junction-based self-shunted superconducting flux qubit with high anharmonicity
authors: Tokunoshin Uchida, Shingo Nozaki, Daiki Kurihara, Hiroki Kutsuma, Shotaro Shirai, Atsushi Noguchi, Hirotaka Terai, Taro Yamashita
abstract: We report a demonstration of a self-shunted superconducting flux qubit (SSFQ) as an ultracompact, strongly anharmonic, and long-lifetime qubit by using the full epitaxially grown NbN/AlN/NbN Josephson junctions. The NbN-junction-based SSFQ achieved a high anharmonicity of 797 MHz as well as drastically reduced footprint of the qubit compared to capacitively shunted (C-shunt) flux qubits with a large shunt capacitor. The lifetime of the SSFQ reached 13 - 25 $μ$s, which is comparable to or relatively higher than that of NbN-based C-shunt flux qubits and Al-based flux qubits with more than 10 times smaller junctions. This indicates that the large epitaxial NbN-based junction can be adopted for SSFQ as well as merged-element transmon with the relatively large junctions. The results presented in this work will offer a new choice of the scalable qubits as well as the material platform toward the realization of large-scale superconducting quantum computers.
summary: The authors experimentally demonstrated a novel self-shunted superconducting flux qubit (SSFQ) built using epitaxial NbN Josephson junctions. This qubit achieves high anharmonicity and long coherence times while maintaining a much smaller physical footprint than conventional designs. The results suggest that large epitaxial junctions are viable for scalable superconducting quantum computer architectures.
main_problem: Developing scalable superconducting qubits that overcome integration bottlenecks and low anharmonicity limitations found in existing architectures.
main_result: The self-shunted superconducting flux qubit (SSFQ) demonstrated high anharmonicity (797 MHz) and a long lifetime (up to 25 $\mu$s) using epitaxial NbN junctions, while significantly reducing the device footprint.
method: The study employed microwave spectroscopy and time-domain measurements using a VNA and QCS to characterize the qubit's energy levels and coherence.
model_or_system: The physical system is an epitaxial NbN-junction-based SSFQ coupled to a readout resonator. The behavior is analyzed using a Hamiltonian describing the qubit, resonator, and coupling.
key_observables: Anharmonicity ($\mathcal{A}$), energy relaxation time ($T_1$), coherence time ($T_{2E}$), and the qubit frequency ($f_{01}$).
important_parameters: High anharmonicity (797 MHz), long lifetime ($\sim 25 \ \mu$s), and a drastically reduced footprint compared to C-shunt qubits.
main_assumptions: The large epitaxial NbN junction size is assumed to be suitable for SSFQ applications, and the system dynamics are modeled by Hamiltonian diagonalization.
figures_summary: Figures show the schematic circuit, spectroscopy ($S_{11}$ phase vs. frequency/flux), and time-domain decay profiles ($T_1$ and $T_2^*$) used to extract qubit parameters.
paper_structure: The paper details the fabrication process, describes the measurement setup (spectroscopy and time-domain), presents the spectroscopic measurements to extract parameters, and finally reports coherence time measurements to validate the qubit performance.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the hardware realization of superconducting qubits, providing crucial experimental data on anharmonicity and coherence times for solid-state quantum computation platforms.
